title: ReplicateBE.jl cannot represent a negative subject-by-formulation correlation, which FDA's FA0(2) permits
raised_by: PR #62, first gating run of the nine synthetic full-replicate cases
effect_on_be_stats: none on any computed value. It bounds where the tier-3 oracle is usable: two of the nine synthetic cases are excluded from the comparison, by a criterion measured from the oracle's own reported parameters rather than from whether the comparison passed.

what_was_observed.agreeing_cases: Seven of nine agree to 1e-6 on all five covariance parameters, on the standard error and on the denominator df.
what_was_observed.the_pattern: The two disagreeing cases are EXACTLY the two where be-stats fits a negative subject-by-formulation correlation. Every case with rho >= 0 agrees. No other property separates them - B is unbalanced and incomplete, D is balanced and complete.

cause.mechanism: ReplicateBE parameterises the correlation through a link, `rholink = :psigmoid`, whose range excludes negative values. Reaching zero requires sending its parameter to minus infinity, and 1e-14 is what the optimiser returns when it tries. Those values are not small numbers; they are zero as that link can express it.
cause.why_be_stats_is_not_similarly_constraine: FDA specifies TYPE=FA0(2), which is G = LL' with L = [[l11, 0], [l21, l22]], giving sigma_BTBR = l11*l21. l21 is unconstrained in sign, so a negative subject-by-formulation covariance is inside the model FDA specifies. This package implements that parameterisation directly.
cause.which_is_right_about_the_model: FDA's. A negative subject-by-formulation covariance is admissible under FA0(2) and under the CSH and UNR alternatives FDA names, and the constraint is the oracle's, not the model's.

how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.route: The classical subject-level analysis - the one-sample analysis of per-subject (mean log T - mean log R) averaged over sequences. No mixed model, no REML, no optimiser, no covariance structure, no Satterthwaite formula.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.applies_to: Case D, which is balanced, complete and interior. PR #62 established that Appendix C reduces to this analysis exactly under those three conditions.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.reading: A third route sharing code with neither implementation agrees with be-stats to eight decimal places and differs from the oracle by 3.2%. The exclusion therefore rests on a number rather than on a reading of ReplicateBE's source.
how_the_disagreement_was_adjudicated.case_b_has_no_third_route: It is incomplete, so the identity does not apply. Its exclusion rests on the same pinned rho, and on the pattern being established across both cases rather than fitted to one.

what_was_not_done.no_tolerance_was_loosened: The gate is unchanged at 0.01 percentage points on each confidence limit. Widening it until B and D passed would have required about 0.6 percentage points, which would also have admitted a genuine defect.
what_was_not_done.no_case_was_dropped_for_disagreeing: The exclusion criterion is a conjunction of two measured properties - be-stats rho clearly below zero AND the oracle's rho collapsed below its link's limit - and a test asserts that exactly the cases meeting it are excluded. A case where the oracle merely fitted a small positive correlation would still be compared.
what_was_not_done.the_criterion_is_reversible: If a future ReplicateBE release reported a negative rho, these cases would re-enter the comparison automatically.

consequence: The oracle is usable for fully replicate designs with a non-negative fitted subject-by-formulation correlation. That covers EMA Data set I, which is the regulator-published case, and seven of the nine synthetic ones. It does not cover negative-correlation fits, which no oracle available to this project can check.
